title: Sto. Nino cowpea (Sto. Niño): Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaTitle: Sto. Nino cowpea: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaDescription: Sto. Nino cowpea is a cowpea variety. 46 to 48 days to harvest, 7.6 t/ha in trials. See its ratings and traits. Compare it with others.
excerpt: Sto. Nino is a registered cowpea variety, also sold or known as Sto. Niño or Santo Niño cowpea. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council in 1995 as NSIC 1995 Cp 06. It takes 46 to 48 days from sowing to the first harvest, with 7.56 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: If you came here looking for Sto. Niño or Santo Niño cowpea, this is the same cowpea. Its seller and farm sources add notes, listed at the end. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for legumes](/land-preparation/legume-land-preparation).

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

Sto. Nino cowpea takes 46 to 48 days from sowing to the first harvest. That is 6.3 days faster than the average of the 13 cowpea varieties with a day count, 53.3 days. A shorter crop frees the field sooner and dodges more of the weather, while a longer one often fills more.

Its average yield of 7.56 t/ha beats the average of its group, 5.44. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing. Its seller gives first harvest 46 to 48 days, last harvest about 74 days.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?

blocks.caption: Reactions in trials, rated under natural field conditions

blocks.text: The pests and diseases that hit cowpea fields most often: [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose), [bean fly](/pests/bean-fly), [legume pod borer](/pests/legume-pod-borer). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
Its pods grew about 20.65 cm long. A hundred seeds weigh about 15.93 grams, so the higher this number, the bigger the seed. The seed coat is light brown.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Yield:** 7.4 t/ha dry season, 7.8 t/ha wet season in registration trials.
**Fruit:** Dark green pods about 20 cm, light brown seeds, about 15 to 16 g per 100 seeds.
Highly tolerant to fusarium wilt, rust and mosaic virus.
Moderately tolerant to aphids and cutworm.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: IPB UPLB cowpea in the NSIC registry, listed for both wet and dry seasons, current seed sellers not confirmed. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant Sto. Nino cowpea

It is recommended for both the wet and the dry season. Cowpea fits the dry season after rice, on the moisture the paddy keeps. Pick by use: green pods for vegetables, or dry seed. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng gulay](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-gulay).

items: Buy sealed packs or tagged sacks from an accredited dealer, and check the packing date and germination rate.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.

items.q: Is Sto. Niño the same as Sto. Nino?
items.a: Yes. Sto. Niño is another name for Sto. Nino, registered as NSIC 1995 Cp 06. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.

items.q: How long does it take to harvest?
items.a: It takes 46 to 48 days from sowing to the first harvest. Then the weather and your care decide the exact day.
The record shows 7.56 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Sto. Nino?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
